clue.text: Girl with skin like velvit?

parts.note: Miss is the title of a young unmarried woman, so stands for a girl
a pelt is an animal's skin or hide

explanation.surface: Someone admires a young woman whose complexion is as soft as velvet.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue deliberately prints 'velvit' with a wrong letter, and that faulty word is itself the definition: it is what a word looks like when spelt wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvit is velvet written with an error, so something like it is wrongly spelt.

clue.text: Film star embraced many men in the main

definitions.meaning: the Hollywood actress famous for her suggestive wit

definitions.text: embraced many men in the main
definitions.meaning: the inflatable life jacket named after her, worn by airmen ditched in the sea, the main

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea; RAF airmen called their life jackets by the star's name because of her figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was a famous Hollywood star, and her name was given to the airmen's inflatable life jacket.

clue.text: Girl appeal

definitions.meaning: to appeal or petition, as in suing for peace

explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a girl's name, and to sue is to plead or petition, an appeal.

clue.text: Say, complete fence to hold down a pest in the chateau

indicators.note: in a down answer the fence sits on top of the next letter, holding it down
say indicates the next word is taken as spoken, by sound

parts.note: to fill something is to complete it, as in filling a form
an oxer is a show-jumping fence, originally a hedge with a rail to stop oxen

explanation.surface: Someone proposes building a full fence to keep down a vineyard pest.
explanation.walkthrough: Phylloxera is an aphid that devastated French vineyards, hence 'in the chateau'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phylloxera is an aphid-like insect that attacks grapevine roots, the great pest of French wine estates.

clue.text: City playboy regularly takes partners

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of playboy

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: An urban playboy routinely picks up companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'playboy' gives LYO; N and S sit opposite each other as partners in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyons is the traditional English spelling of Lyon, the large French city.

clue.text: Imaginary beast makes frightening noise — almost start

parts.note: boo is the cry made to startle someone

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to start is to jump with surprise

explanation.surface: A creature conjured up by imagination lets out a scary sound that nearly makes you jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boojum is Lewis Carroll's invented creature in The Hunting of the Snark, a fantastical animal.

clue.text: On Derby Day, select first places via these?

definitions.text: On Derby Day, select first places via these?

indicators.note: first places points to the opening letter of each of the first four words

explanation.surface: Racegoers on Derby Day pick likely winners by looking at the betting prices.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'On Derby Day select' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes how punters choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the bookmakers' prices, which bettors consult to pick horses likely to come first.

clue.text: At end of country, bookmaker takes old coins

parts.note: John wrote a book of the Bible, so he is a book maker
groats were old English silver coins worth four pence

explanation.surface: At the far edge of the land a turf accountant pockets some antique money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' suggests a betting firm, but it is John, author of a Gospel. John o' Groats is the traditional far northern tip of mainland Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: John o' Groats is the village at the north-eastern tip of Scotland, the end of the country.

clue.text: Handle tailless animal I held above river

indicators.note: in a down answer, above means the first part sits over the next
held means the shortened animal holds the letter I inside
tailless means the animal loses its final letter

parts.note: a monkey is an animal

explanation.surface: A tailless creature is gripped by its handle and lifted over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' is slang for a name, not a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is a name or nickname, and a handle is slang for exactly that.

clue.text: Big letter held gift

indicators.note: held means the big word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: big and large mean the same
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: An oversized letter contained a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, money or presents freely bestowed, so a gift.

clue.text: Occasionally each gets present: what next?

parts.note: each and every mean the same here
the present moment is now
'and then?' is how one asks what happens next

explanation.surface: Someone receives gifts only from time to time and wonders what is coming next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the time sense, now; the closing query 'what next?' supplies the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for at irregular intervals, from time to time, meaning occasionally.

clue.text: Both sides are bound to agree by it

definitions.text: Both sides are bound to agree by it

parts.words: Both sides are bound to agree by it
parts.note: sounds like a treaty or negotiation, but describes the mathematical symbol that forces the two halves of an equation to balance

explanation.surface: A treaty clause obliges two negotiating parties to come to terms.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the expressions on either side of this symbol must have equal value, so the sides agree.

clue.text: Jack specifically works so, improving the tone?

definitions.meaning: a car jack does its job by raising things
describing something that lifts the spirits or raises moral standards

explanation.definitionFit: A jack works by raising up loads, and something done in an elevating manner morally improves the tone.

clue.text: Con man

definitions.meaning: to con is to swindle or cheat someone
a man is a piece in chess, and the castle-shaped piece is one

explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle, and the rook is a chess piece, which chess players call a man.

clue.text: Pretenders to the crown, and more besides

definitions.text: Pretenders to the crown, and more besides

parts.words: Pretenders to the crown, and more besides
parts.note: reads as royal claimants, but describes dentures, which fake teeth including crowns and others besides

explanation.surface: Rival claimants to the throne, and plenty of other people too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are artificial teeth that pretend to be real ones, crowns among them.

clue.text: Quickly contacted boy about English and Roman law

indicators.note: about means the boy's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name, short for Edward
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A lad gets in touch fast about English and Roman legal matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Lex is the Latin for law, hence 'Roman law'.
explanation.definitionFit: To telex someone was to send a message by teleprinter, a fast way of contacting before email.

clue.text: Dish out dirt a spy spins

indicators.note: dish out means hand around, so the letters of dirt a spy are distributed afresh

explanation.surface: A gossip spreads scandal that a secret agent has fabricated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish out' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the definition is 'spins', short pleasure trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short drive or outing for pleasure, and day trips are excursions of that kind.

clue.text: East-end bird one ringed in practice?

definitions.meaning: the London cockney pronunciation of sparrow, East End being cockney territory
a boxer who spars, in the boxing ring for practice rather than a real fight

explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is the home of cockney speech, which turns 'sparrow' into this. 'ringed' suggests a bird ringed by ornithologists, but it is a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney speech renders sparrow this way, and a boxer practising in the ring is one who spars.

clue.text: Man, with judge and jury at last accepting fine, free to slip off

indicators.note: accepting means the judge and jury letters take in the following pieces
at last picks the final letter of jury
slip off suggests the letters of free sliding out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A man in court, with the judge and the jury at last taking a fine, is free to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip off' is the anagram signal: being free to slip off sounds like leaving court, but it shuffles the fine and the free; 'Man' is the bare definition, a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey is a man's first name, so it can stand for a man in crossword terms.

clue.text: About to leave sailor, a drunken tar in Eastern capital

indicators.note: about to leave means the abbreviation for about is removed

parts.note: Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a name for a sailor
c, for circa, is the abbreviation for about

indicators.note: drunken means the letters of tar stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk seaman is on the point of leaving his ship for a night out in an Asian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to leave' seems to mean 'on the point of leaving', but it removes C from JACK. 'drunken' rearranges TAR to RTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia, in the East.

clue.text: Bind new leaves around noon

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the noon letter
new tells us the letters of leaves are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ties up fresh foliage at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges LEAVES to ESLAVE, which goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave is to bind someone in servitude, to make them a captive.

clue.text: Raised railway above unfinished road leading to studios

indicators.note: in a down answer, above means the railway sits over the road

parts.note: the el is the American term for an elevated railway

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a street is a road

explanation.surface: An overhead railway runs above an incomplete road heading to the film studios.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree, north of London, is home to famous film and television studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree is the Hertfordshire town known for its film and television studios, a byword for them.

clue.text: End of chain caught in gear link

indicators.note: caught in means that letter is held inside the word for gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of chain

explanation.surface: The final link of a bicycle chain gets stuck in the gears.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join or unite closely, as broken bones knit together, so to link.

clue.text: Does a smashing experiment the wrong way, in grossly stupid case

indicators.note: in, with case, says the stupid word holds the other letters inside it
case paired with in means the stupid word encloses the rest

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid or insensitive

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the are put in a wrong order

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A scientist conducts a destructive experiment incorrectly, in what is a hopelessly foolish matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 'the' before the street abbreviation joins them; 'in ... case' means the stupid word encases both. The surface's 'wrong way' is one phrase, but its words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash test smashes a vehicle into a barrier deliberately, so one carrying them does a smashing experiment.

clue.text: A selection of points as promised

parts.note: SW, south-west, is a compass point
or offers a choice between alternatives, a selection
N, north, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Some chosen points are stated as pledged.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'SW or N', a choice of compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Sworn means bound by an oath, as one has promised.

clue.text: African's last letter to be broadcast

definitions.meaning: read as 'African is', a member of a people of southern Africa
the final letter of the radio spelling alphabet, used in broadcasting

explanation.definitionFit: The Zulu are a southern African people, and Zulu is the code word for Z in radio communication.

clue.text: For Sir's super-ego is dented by prestigious chairman?

indicators.note: something dented is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and all four letters are used

explanation.surface: An eminent man's inflated self-image takes a knock from someone of high standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dented' rearranges FOR SIRS SUPEREGO into the answer; 'chairman' is a play on holding a university chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Regius Professor holds a royally founded chair at an old university, a prestigious holder of a chair.

clue.text: Half-term drink

indicators.note: half takes the first half of the word

parts.note: a term or period of time, such as the cricket season

explanation.surface: During the school half-term holiday someone has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-term' suggests the school holiday; 'the drink' is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal slang for the sea, as in falling into the drink.

clue.text: Note poor area hosting opening of youth hostel

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: hosting means the slum word takes the next letter in

parts.note: a slum is a squalid run-down district

indicators.note: opening of picks the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: A message notes that a deprived district is home to a newly opened youth hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a refuge or shelter, an older sense close to a hostel for those in need.

clue.text: Rudimentary action he messed up

indicators.note: messed up means the letters of action he are jumbled

explanation.surface: He made a mess of something done in a primitive way.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only begun and not fully formed, hence rudimentary or undeveloped.
